https://www.barrons.com/articles/amazons-new-promise-is-alexa-everywhere-1537474862 Amazon’s New Promise Is ‘Alexa Everywhere’ By Sept. 20, 2018 4:21 p.m. ET Text Size Medium Large Amazon’s updated Echo Dot, one of 14 new devices that Amazon announced on Thursday. Photo: courtesy of Amazon By Sept. 20, 2018 4:21 p.m. ET
Amazon (AMZN) is planning a new wave in its home invasion.
An avalanche of Echo devices for the home, built around and connected to its virtual assistant Alexa, landed Thursday in a press event at the company’s urban botanical garden complex in Seattle.
A redesigned Echo Dot led the parade of 14 voice-controlled devices that include a microwave oven, clock, amplifiers, and an in-car gadget. The company also unfurled security cameras.
The enhanced lineup signals Amazon’s serious ambitions for the connected home, considered crucial to its success in the smart speaker market, which is expected to top $30 billion by 2024, according to Global Market Insights. The market was $4.5 billion last year.
Underscoring the company’s intent, Tom Taylor, senior vice president for Amazon Alexa, said in a press release today : “We want you to have access to Alexa everywhere—in your kitchen, in your living room, in your office, and now in your car or truck.”
Amazon shares closed up 0.9% today to $1,944.
The slate of new Alexa-enabled devices comes several months after Amazon acquired Ring, maker of video doorbells, for more than $1 billion. Amazon has also reportedly been developing a home robot , according to Bloomberg.
It remains unclear how commercially successful the new devices will be. In a similar event a year ago, Amazon introduced new Alexa and Echo devices that included a smart alarm clock, digital home hub, hockey puck-shaped devices consumers can use to play games, and an Amazon Fire TV that supports 4K technology.
Amazon’s latest batch of gadgets pits it squarely against Sonos (SONO) in the home-audio market. Sonos, a pioneer in multi-room audio, went public in August. Its stock fell 3.1% in the wake of the Amazon announcement, and it’s now down 7% since the IPO. Apple (AAPL) and Alphabet ’s (GOOGL) Google are increasingly devoting their attention to home audio products, as well.
In the coming year, Amazon could even find itself competing with General Electric (GE), which already makes an Alexa-compatible smart microwave. Most Popular
